title: Using Virtual Reality Based Mindfulness and Self-Compassion to Improve Mental Health in Hemodialysis
official: "Toujours Dimanche": A Nature-Based Mindfulness and Self-Compassion Meditation Program Delivered Through Immersive Virtual Reality During Hemodialysis. A Pilot Randomized Controlled Feasibility Trial
summary:
The goal of this pilot clinical trial is to learn whether a virtual reality mindfulness and self-compassion program can be used during hemodialysis, whether patients find it acceptable, and whether it is safe. The study will include 26 adults who have received in-center hemodialysis for at least 3 months at Hôpital du Haut-Richelieu in Quebec, Canada.

The program, called "Toujours Dimanche," combines guided meditation with videos and sounds of nature. Participants wear a virtual reality headset that makes them feel surrounded by natural landscapes. Mindfulness means paying attention to the present moment without judgment. Self-compassion means treating yourself with kindness during difficult experiences.

The main questions are:

Can researchers recruit patients, and can patients complete the planned virtual reality sessions?

How do patients feel about the program, and how well does it fit into their dialysis treatments?

Does the program cause unwanted effects, such as nausea, dizziness, or discomfort?

Researchers will also collect information about anxiety, depression, stress, emotional well-being, physical symptoms, quality of life, and physical activity. This small pilot study is not designed to determine whether the program improves these outcomes. Its findings will help researchers plan a larger trial.

Participants will be assigned by chance to one of two groups, with an equal chance of joining either group:

Virtual reality group: Participants will use the headset during their regular hemodialysis treatments for 20 minutes, twice a week, for 16 weeks. Each session includes 10 minutes of guided meditation followed by 10 minutes of freely exploring the virtual nature setting. A research team member will help participants use the equipment and will be available during sessions.

Comparison group: Participants will receive an educational brochure about caring for their mental health during hemodialysis. They will be offered free access to the virtual reality program after the study.

Participants in both groups will:

* Complete questionnaires before the program, around its midpoint, at its end, and about 10 weeks after it ends.
* Wear a wrist-worn activity tracker to record their steps, including for 2 weeks before the program begins.

After the final data collection, a sample of patients and nurses will take part in interviews to share their experiences with the program and suggest improvements before a larger study.

The research team will ask participants in the virtual reality group about their comfort and emotional well-being before and after each session. The team will also monitor blood pressure and other unwanted effects during dialysis.

Study participation will last about 28 to 34 weeks, including initial assessments, the 16-week program, and follow-up. Virtual reality sessions will take place during regular dialysis treatments and will not require extra trips.

Researchers will compare the two groups to explore changes in the outcomes measured and assess how practical the study procedures are. They will also interview dialysis staff to understand how the program could fit into routine care.

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults aged 18 years or older receiving in-center hemodialysis.
* Able to provide informed consent in French or English.
* Able to follow the study procedures.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Uncontrolled migraine, epilepsy, or vertigo.
* Planned transition to peritoneal dialysis or home hemodialysis, transfer to another dialysis center, or living-donor kidney transplantation within the next 4 months.
* Hospitalization within the past 30 days.
* Fewer than two hemodialysis sessions per week.
* Glaucoma or recovery from recent eye surgery.
* Currently receiving psychotherapy.
* Uncontrolled anxiety, depression, or psychosis.
* Recent bereavement or a traumatic life event.
* Presence of a pacemaker, due to potential interference with the virtual reality headset.
